title: What If Every Hippo Vanished? Rivers Would Lose Their Glass

scenes.text: What if every hippo vanished? East Africa's rivers would lose a hidden supply of glass.
Hippos graze grass on land at night, then spend the day wallowing in rivers.
In Kenya's Mara River, their droppings deliver about 880 pounds of silica a day, over three quarters of the river's supply.
Tiny algae called diatoms build glass shells from that silica, and diatoms feed the river's food web.
Without hippos that conveyor belt stops. Yet their waste also drained the oxygen from the water enough to kill fish thirteen times in one study.
So the river would change in both directions. The pools would empty, and its chemistry would shift with them.
